summary: H.J. Res. 35 is a joint resolution that disapproves and nullifies an Environmental Protection Agency rule concerning a waste emissions charge for petroleum and natural gas systems, effectively eliminating the annual waste emissions charge on certain oil or gas facilities under the Methane Emissions Reduction Program.

affected_groups.effect: They are relieved from the annual waste emissions charge for exceeding greenhouse gas and methane emission thresholds under the nullified EPA rule.
The agency's specific rule regarding waste emissions charge procedures, netting, and exemptions is voided and cannot be enforced.

key_provisions: Expresses congressional disapproval of the EPA rule titled Waste Emissions Charge for Petroleum and Natural Gas Systems: Procedures for Facilitating Compliance, Including Netting and Exemptions.
Makes the specified EPA rule have no force or effect.
Eliminates the annual waste emissions charge on oil or gas facilities under the Methane Emissions Reduction Program.
missing_information: The source text does not specify the exact financial amounts of the eliminated waste emissions charges.
The source text does not provide estimates of the total number of facilities affected.
summary_detail.plain_summary: H.J. Res. 35 is a joint resolution that disapproves and nullifies an Environmental Protection Agency rule concerning a waste emissions charge for petroleum and natural gas systems, effectively eliminating the annual waste emissions charge on certain oil or gas facilities under the Methane Emissions Reduction Program.
summary_detail.significance: The joint resolution completely voids a specific federal regulatory rule issued by the EPA on November 18, 2024, halting the collection of associated waste emissions charges from oil and gas facilities.
